blocks.text: Unusually detailed docstring documents who calls the route, what a grant does (raises per-run ceiling, not account pool), the 11-step order and why the atomic claim is step 8, and why runs.transition is used instead of run_manager. Also documents the error body contract.
blocks.title: Module docstring: protocol, semantics, and claim ordering

blocks.text: GrantServices is a dataclass of callables (not module-level globals) so tests can inject fakes. get_services() assembles the real collaborators: usage_ledger.check, metering.RunBudgetStore, RunCeilingPolicy, and lazy lookups for registry/handlers/emitter.
blocks.title: GrantServices and get_services

blocks.text: _fail builds an HTTPException with a fixed code/message dict. _thread runs a sync function in asyncio.to_thread. _spawn fires a task and holds a reference in _background to prevent GC mid-run. _bearer extracts the token from an Authorization: Bearer header, returning None for anything else.
blocks.title: Small helpers: fail constructor, threading, background spawn, bearer extraction

blocks.text: grant_run_credits delegates entirely to _grant, catching any unforeseen exception before the claim as a 503. require_device is the FastAPI dependency that verifies the device JWT; a device store fault is 503, not 401, because nothing should be allowed on a guess.
blocks.title: Route entry point and device auth dependency

blocks.anchor: async def _own_run(user_id: str, device_id: str, run_id: str) -> "runs.Run":
blocks.text: _own_run fetches and ownership-checks the run. _pool_with_room calls the ledger with fail-closed semantics. _grant orchestrates steps 2–11: run fetch, state check, device connectivity, pool check, buffer existence, credit numbers, atomic claim, then ceiling write/emitter bind/state announcement/hook spawn. _undo reverses post-claim writes if anything after step 8 fails.
blocks.title: Grant logic: steps 2–11

blocks.anchor: async def _undo(services: GrantServices, emitter, run: "runs.Run", previous: "float | None", was_bound: bool) -> None:
blocks.text: _undo runs all three rollback steps (restore ceiling, unbind emitter if newly bound, transition back to paused_budget) even when earlier steps fail, logging each error separately so a partial rollback doesn't mask the original failure.
blocks.title: _undo: post-claim rollback

gotchas: Pool check is fail-closed (503) unlike most of the codebase's fail-open posture — a grant on a pool that cannot be read could over-commit credits
The claim is step 8 of 11 by design: everything before it only reads, so a failure before the claim changes nothing
_undo tries every step even if an earlier step fails, to maximize the chance of getting the run back to a retryable state
Response bodies never echo the input token, paths, or exception text — only state words, credit numbers, and timestamps
how_it_works: require_device extracts and verifies the device JWT from the Authorization header; 401 on bad token, 503 on device store unavailability
_own_run fetches the run and checks both user_id and device_id match — any mismatch is a 404, same as not found
_pool_with_room calls services.check to verify the user's credit pool has room; a pool that cannot be read is a 503 (fail closed, unlike most of this codebase)
runs.transition atomically moves the run from paused_budget to running with a parallel-run cap; 409 if someone else moved it first, 429 if the cap is hit
On success: ceiling written to Redis, run_guard.grant_more called, emitter re-bound, state_changed/budget_granted emitted, on_resume hooks fired as a background task
_undo restores the ceiling, unbinds the emitter if this request bound it, and transitions the run back to paused_budget if any post-claim step fails
outputs: GrantResponse with state, run_credit_ceiling, run_credits_spent, granted_credits
purpose: Implements the terminal-side "grant more credits" flow for M2C runs that stopped at their per-run credit ceiling. Accepts only device JWTs (not web session tokens), verifies the run belongs to both the account and the device, checks pool headroom, atomically transitions the run from paused_budget to running, then raises the ceiling and re-binds the emitter. Undoes all post-claim writes if any step after the claim fails.
side_effects: run_guard.grant_more call (clears breaker and cancel flag)
on_resume hooks fired as asyncio background task
summary: POST /v1/code/runs/{run_id}/grant: raises the credit ceiling on a paused-budget M2C run and restarts it, authenticated by device JWT.
